signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Yield Spread
signals.text: USD/SEK trades at 9.829, sitting above its SMA20 at 9.667, SMA50 at 9.608, and SMA200 at 9.363, reflecting a firm technical position on the back of broad dollar strength. The G10 currency strength scorecard places USD as the leading performer with a 1W average of +0.948% across nine pairs, while SEK sits at the bottom as the laggard at -0.716% across two pairs, creating a wide bilateral spread of 1.664%. This performance divergence aligns with the economic surprise index where SEK registers -29.2 for persistent data misses, contrasted with a robust US Treasury yield curve where the 10-year yield has climbed to 5.104% and the 2-year yield trades at 4.760%. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; broad dollar outperformance and Swedish growth deceleration support the bilateral spread. Catalyst: US initial jobless claims and durable goods orders on Thursday. Risk: US 10-year yields retreat below 5.00% and macroeconomic data softens, compressing the bilateral spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Differential + Rate Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.32, holding above its SMA20 at 156.61 while testing below its SMA50 at 158.85 and SMA200 at 158.42. The OIS overnight benchmark rate differential shows SOFR at 3.85% versus TONA at 0.9770%, maintaining a wide 287bp carry advantage that anchors the pair's underlying bid despite broader equity headwinds and a S&P 500 decline of 0.82%. Options markets price a 1M ATM implied volatility of 7.5% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.8%, resulting in a -2.3% volatility risk premium that highlights an unusual options complacency. The 25-delta risk reversal prints a notable put skew at -2.32, reflecting heavy hedging demand for downside protection even as spot prices grind higher on the rate differential. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage and rate divergence sustain the bid while VIX remains contained at 15.2. Catalyst: BoJ trimmed mean and weighted median core CPI data on Thursday. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a rapid unwinding of carry positions across JPY crosses.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Vol + Technical Resistance
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1378, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1576, SMA50 at 1.1542, and SMA200 at 1.1630 after sliding 0.66% intraday following strong US business activity data. CFTC leveraged funds report a net short of 51,355 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 32, while retail sentiment shows a strong long bias with 71% of retail accounts positioned on the buy side, creating a clear divergence between institutional positioning and retail participation. Options data reveals a 1M ATM implied volatility of 5.3% alongside a 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, producing a positive volatility risk premium of +0.6% and a mild put skew in the 25-delta risk reversal at -0.51. Trade bias: Short EUR/USD; technical breakdown below moving average clusters and positive VRP favor continued downside pressure. Catalyst: US initial jobless claims and durable goods orders on Thursday. Risk: EUR/USD reclaims the SMA50 at 1.1542, invalidating the bearish technical structure.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + Retail Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5665, extending a 1.17% daily decline and sitting well below its SMA20 at 0.5830, SMA50 at 0.5854, and SMA200 at 0.5855. CFTC leveraged funds maintain a net short position of 2,319 contracts at the 44th percentile of its 52-week range, while retail sentiment registers an extreme long bias at 89%, showing retail traders heavily fading the institutional positioning and ongoing spot weakness. The OIS rate differential shows SOFR at 3.85% versus the RBNZ overnight rate at 2.75%, maintaining a 125bp carry advantage in favor of the US dollar. Economic surprise index data for New Zealand stands at +8.8, reflecting modest positive data surprises that fail to offset the broader dollar rally driven by US Treasury yield surges. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; retail extreme long positioning combined with negative technical momentum points toward further liquidation. Catalyst: US initial jobless claims on Thursday. Risk: NZD/USD breaks back above the SMA20 at 0.5830, signaling a squeeze of leveraged short positions.
